title: Add bit-channel analysis for per-bit LLR statistics and information metrics
description:
Add explicit bit-channel analysis support so the modem framework can analyze reliability differences between bit positions within a symbol. This story covers per-bit LLR distributions, demapper-mode semantics, and information metrics such as MI and GMI, while keeping analysis strictly opt-in.

## Background

For QAM and other higher-order constellations, different bit positions inside one symbol can have different reliability. The modem framework therefore needs more than just correct map and demap behavior: it must expose bit positions as analyzable channels, make demapper approximations explicit, and provide tools for per-bit LLR and information-metric analysis.

This analysis capability must not slow down ordinary simulations. Many production or regression runs will not request bit-channel analysis, so the hot modem and simulation paths must remain unchanged in behavior and performance when analysis is disabled.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] The framework exposes bit-position and bit-channel identity explicitly enough to analyze different bits within one symbol.
- [ ] Demapper semantics used for analysis are explicit, including whether the analysis path uses exact log-MAP, max-log, or another supported approximation.
- [ ] Analysis tools can compute or export per-bit conditional LLR statistics and distributions, including $p(L_k \mid B_k = 0)$ and $p(L_k \mid B_k = 1)$.
- [ ] Analysis tools can estimate per-bit mutual information or GMI for supported modem paths.
- [ ] Bit-channel analysis is opt-in and does not impose measurable overhead, extra allocations, or analysis-specific work on simulations that do not request it.

## Notes

This story is about observability and research tooling around the modem framework, not about creating a second modem implementation. It must rely on the shared modem source of truth.
